title: Automated Emergency Dispatch Voice Triage
business: Emergency medical dispatch centers handling high volumes of inbound distress calls.
problem: Human dispatchers struggle to maintain composure and accuracy during complex, multi-step triage protocols while simultaneously documenting patient symptoms in real-time.
solution: The GPT-Realtime-2.1 model leverages its reasoning capabilities and tool use to conduct voice-based triage, guiding callers through standardized medical protocols while executing database lookups to verify patient history or local hospital capacity.
steps: Establish a persistent connection via the v1/realtime endpoint to enable low-latency, bidirectional audio streaming.
Define custom function tools that allow the model to query external medical databases for patient records.
Configure the model's reasoning effort parameter to balance the depth of clinical analysis against the need for immediate, conversational response.
Implement interruption handling to allow the model to pause its current instruction if the caller provides urgent, clarifying information.
Stream the final triage summary to the dispatch console via tool output, ensuring the human dispatcher receives structured data.
outcome: Improved consistency in triage protocol adherence and reduced cognitive load on dispatchers, allowing them to focus on high-level coordination rather than manual data entry.
limitation: Configurable reasoning effort can introduce latency; if the model is set to high reasoning, the conversational flow may experience delays that are unsuitable for critical, time-sensitive emergency interactions. This can be checked by monitoring the time-to-first-token during high-stress simulation scenarios.
